title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: an axiomatic, combinatorial foundation for 'spaces' and 'figures' in the 1986 'Ateliers' notes. The neighbouring pages give the objects and conventions.

(i) Sigma_A (or Sigma_U) is a complete lattice of 'parts' (spatial loci). It has a least element (empty set) and a greatest element. It carries a complement C, which is an anti-involution exchanging Inf and Sup. It also carries a disjointness/orthogonality relation |o|, with S |o| S' iff S is contained in C S'.

(ii) From a set A of 'elements' with figures F and a datum Delta, one singles out a subfamily Sigmacons_A of 'constructible' parts.

This page makes four points.
(1) Sigmacons_A is in general not stable under Sup, Inf or complement. This is the familiar situation in which the constructible loci one generates do not form a sub-Boolean-algebra or sublattice.
(2) In place of such closure properties, Grothendieck announces an 'axiome des supports'. It involves an additional structure written C-check (Č) and is to be stated and verified later.
(3) Notation. For X in A, X° = supp°(X) is defined as the smallest S in Sigma_A such that X belongs to S. It exists because Sigma_A is closed under arbitrary Inf. Grothendieck asserts that it lies in Sigmacons_A. In modern terms, X ↦ X° is the closure (hull) operator of the Moore family Sigma_A evaluated on a point: the 'support' of X.
(4) Interpretation: this makes precise the intuition of the minimal stratum (or its closure) attached to a given stratum X. This is analogous to the closure of a point in an Alexandrov/specialization topology, or the closure of a stratum in a stratification satisfying the frontier condition.

The next page uses this to define Dep(X) = {X'° | X' in X~}, the 'spatial unfolding' of X. Dep(X) is a set of mutually disjoint supports with largest element X°, ordered isomorphically to X~. It thereby links the order << to the supports, with the S in Sigma_A behaving like <<-closed subsets of A.
errors: The claim that supp°(X) belongs to Sigmacons_A (and not merely to Sigma_A) is asserted, not proved. It presumably depends on the yet-unstated 'axiome des supports' or on how constructible parts are generated. This is a gap at this stage, not an error.
The axiome des supports itself is only announced; its content (involving the structure Č) is deferred.

ideas.what: Smallest element of a family of parts closed under arbitrary intersections that contains a given element: the support/closure of a point
ideas.modern_name: closure operator of a Moore family; closure of a point (specialization order / Alexandrov topology)
ideas.where_published: Analogous support notions are everywhere in EGA/SGA (support of a sheaf, closure of a point in a scheme), but not in this axiomatic form

ideas.what: Constructible parts not closed under lattice operations; compatibility replaced by an 'axiom of supports'
ideas.modern_name: constructible sets / closure-of-strata (frontier) conditions in stratification theory
ideas.where_published: Constructible sets appear in EGA IV; the abstract axiomatics here appear unpublished

ideas.what: Interpretation of supp°(X) as the minimal stratum attached to a given stratum X
ideas.modern_name: closure of a stratum; poset of strata of a stratified space
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in stratification theory (Thom, Mather); stratified spaces discussed in Esquisse d'un programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame/stratified spaces, but not this formalism

missed.claim: An 'axiome des supports' is announced as a substitute for closure of constructible parts under Sup/Inf/complement, involving an extra structure Č. On this page it is neither stated nor verified. It belongs to an unpublished axiomatic theory of 'spaces/figures' (Spatios) in which supports and stratifications are derived from a lattice with complement plus figures.
missed.quote: Mais il y a un axiome ("axiome des supports") qui tient lieu d'une telle compatibilité, sur lesquelles nous allons avoir à revenir — et à vérifier
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of mainly historical interest: it documents a 1986 attempt at a synthetic, lattice-theoretic foundation of stratified 'spaces'. It could be compared with later work on posets of strata and exit-path categories. The mathematics on this page itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page only introduces notation: the support of a point as the least closed part containing it, i.e. a standard closure operator. It also announces an axiom without stating it. This is mildly interesting as part of an unpublished foundational project, but there is no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'sur lesquelles nous allons {+avoir+} à revenir' reads more naturally as 'sur laquelle nous allons avoir à revenir'; the closing parenthesis after 'cet axiome' is missing in the transcription.

The final lines likely read: 'C'est une explicitation possible de l'intuition de la strate minimale (underlined) associée à une strate donnée X' rather than '...de la strate associée [?] : une strate domine [?] X'.
'W°X' above which 'supp°(X)' is written: the inserted 'supp°(X)' is the intended notation, and 'W°X' is probably a misreading of the overwritten symbol.
'en général' and 'ni par C' are correct; C denotes the complement operation (∁).
